overview: This Senate resolution honors the teachers who lead career and technical education (CTE) classes, which teach hands-on job skills, and the work-based learning coordinators who connect students with internships, apprenticeships and job shadowing. It points to shortages of CTE teachers in many states and says all students should have access to quality CTE and work-based learning. It also states that CTE teachers, coordinators and educators in every subject deserve competitive pay, good benefits and safe working conditions, and that improving these would help reduce teacher shortages. The Senate approved it on February 26, 2026.
for: Supporters say the resolution draws attention to the educators who make job-training programs possible and to the shortages that leave many schools unable to fill these teaching jobs.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic: it calls for better pay and conditions for teachers but does not change any law or provide any money to achieve that.
